Chapter 20 (al-bāb al-ʿishrūn): On the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn and the answered invocations that belong to it [303]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that among the occult properties of this noble sura is what is related from Anas b. Mālik — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((For everything there is a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is Yā-Sīn. Whoever recites it, God writes for him, for his reciting of it, the reciting of the Qurʾān ten times.)) And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Sūrat Yā-Sīn is called al-Muʿammima (the Enveloping).)) It was said: O Messenger of God, and what is al-Muʿammima? He said: ((It envelops its possessor with good in this world and in the hereafter. And it is called al-Dāfiʿa al-Qāḍiya (the Repelling, the Fulfilling): it repels from its possessor every evil, and fulfils for him every need, and bears on his behalf every trial in this world, and repels from him the terrors of the hereafter.)) And it is related with a sound chain of transmission from Abū Bakr and Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ((Whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn as far as His words And strike for them a similitude: the people of the town (Q 36:13), and then supplicates for something immediately upon it, is answered without fail.)) And it is tried-and-tested (mujarrab): it has been put to the test and proved sound in many places.

And whoever writes Sūrat Yā-Sīn and drinks it — there enter into his belly a thousand remedies, and a thousand lights, and a thousand blessings, and a thousand wisdoms, and a thousand mercies; and every disease and ailment is stripped away from him. So let him write it upon gazelle parchment on a Thursday, in the hour of Jupiter, with the moon increasing in light, and hang it upon the left upper arm: he is made secure from the pain of the spleen.

And it is said that whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn in the graveyard, God lightens [the punishment] for them on that day, and he has good deeds according to the number of those buried in it. And whoever recites it in the evening does not cease to be in joy until the morning; or in the morning, does not cease to be in /fol. 208r./ joy until the evening. And whoever recites it beside a Muslim upon whom death has come down — God sends down, for the number of every letter of it, angels who stand before him in ranks, and pray for him, and ask forgiveness for him, and accompany his funeral bier, and witness his burial. And whatever Muslim recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn before his need, it is fulfilled for him. And whoever recites it while he is fearful is made secure; or hungry, is filled; or thirsty, is given to drink. And whatever Muslim recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn while he is in the throes of death — the angel of death does not seize his spirit until he sees the good pleasure (riḍwān) of the Garden and it is made beloved to him.

And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Truly there is in the Qurʾān a sura that is called "the Mighty" in God's sight, and its possessor is called "the Noble" in God's sight. It will intercede for its reciter on the Day of Resurrection for more than [the tribes of] Rabīʿa and Muḍar; and it is Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān).)) And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Truly there is in the Qurʾān a sura that intercedes for its reciter, and its listener is forgiven — behold, it is Yā-Sīn. And whoever recites it on the day of Friday rises in the morning forgiven.)) And it is related from al-Ḥasan that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever recites Yā-Sīn and Ḥā-Mīm al-Dukhān on the eve of Friday, in faith and in the seeking of reward, is forgiven what has gone before of his sin.))

For battle and for other [purposes]: one recites the istirjāʿ three times — Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we are returning (Q 2:156) — and recites Yā-Sīn. And whoever is a captive, or fearful, or gone astray, or absent, or in debt — let him recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn three times: he is set loose, and made secure, and guided, and brought back, and his debt is discharged. And likewise in all pressing affairs. Or [if he is] fearful or gone astray, he recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn seventy times, and you recite this supplication seven times after the first time; then you recite [it] at every time. And the supplication is this: "O company [of spirits] made subject and obedient to this blessed sura, by the right of the prophets of God and His friends, and by the right of your Creator: make my word to run current, and my speech heard and accepted; and suffice me in my pressing affairs, near and not far off; and supply me and help me in all matters, universal and particular, by the right of It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 27:30). Haste! Speed! This very hour! Truly He is powerful over whatsoever He wills, and worthy to answer."

For an unjust enemy: whoever has an enemy who has wronged him and wishes to destroy him — let him take a mud-brick and set it before him upon the bank of a running river or of a cistern, and let him be facing [the qibla]; and let him recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn forty-one times, and with each time let him draw a line upon that brick. Then, when he has finished the reciting, let him pray over the brick the funeral prayer, and let him make the brick the image of his enemy; then let him cast it into the river or the cistern — for he perishes swiftly. And this is a trust, not to be employed save after grave compulsion and great wronging. So fear God, glorified and exalted is He, and have mercy upon His servant, and dread lest God take vengeance upon you. /fol. 208v./

For the departing of care and of […]: a certain one of the gnostics mentioned that when a man is laden with care he recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and when he has completed it he supplicates with this blessed supplication. He says: "[Glory be to] the Reliever of every care-laden one; glory be to the Bringer of relief to every debtor; glory be to the Deliverer of every prisoner; who has set His treasuries, by His power, between the kāf and the nūn: His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say to it 'Be', and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). O Reliever of care, relieve my care!" He says it three times.

And among the occult properties of this noble sura, for retention: whoever writes the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn with rose-water and saffron, and writes it seven consecutive days, once each day — he retains what he hears, and overcomes whoever disputes with him, and is magnified in the eyes [of men]. And among the occult properties of the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn: it is drunk for the promoting of urine. And whoever gives it as a drink to a nursing woman, there is in it for the suckling child a good nourishment and a complete healing, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon his neck is made secure from evil eyes, and from the jinn, and from vermin, and from pains.

And among the occult properties of this sura, for the destroying of a wrongdoer: al-Kalbī mentioned that there was a man who had killed by mistake, and the next of kin of the slain man charged him with having killed him deliberately, and so kept seeking him out in order to kill him. A certain righteous man said to him: If you are truthful in your account, then recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn before you go out of your house, and go out to meet him; for by God he will not see you, since he is your wronger. And that man used to recite it before going out of his house, and his pursuer would not catch sight of him on his road. I say: and it is soundly established that our master the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — recited the beginning of it when he went out to Quraysh, when they had plotted by night to kill him; and he went out upon them and they did not see him, and he put dust upon their heads.

And a certain one of the righteous — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said in his discourse: And among the things that have been made clear, and whose blessing has been ascertained, is that whoever is in fear of a tyrannical ruler, or of one who seeks him out unjustly, or [upon whom] a need has come knocking, or whose riding-beast has strayed from the road — [it is] that he should recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn and then say: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. In the name of God, other than whom there is no god, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. In the name of God, other than whom there is no god, the Possessor of Majesty and Honour. In the name of

God, with whose name nothing can do harm, neither in the earth nor in the heaven, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. O God, truly I take refuge with You from the evil of So-and-so son of So-and-so." That suffices.

And know that even were the heavens to close down upon the earth, and the world to blaze up in fire with civil strife, and then the servant were to obey his Lord within himself with a truthful taking of refuge — God, exalted is He, would deliver him according to the measure of his sincerity.

And as for His word "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58): it is recited for the fulfilment of needs and the sufficing of pressing affairs, one thousand four hundred and ninety-nine times, and the object sought is obtained, by the leave of God, exalted is He. /fol. 209r./ And for the sufficing against the evil of the night-visitant and of the epidemic: whoever writes "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58) 5 times and hangs it upon himself is kept safe from the visitants of the night and the day. And whoever makes remembrance of it in the days of the epidemic, twenty-eight times every day, is kept safe from the plagues of the epidemic. And from ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ, who said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — [said]: ((Whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn, his needs are fulfilled.)) Al-Dārimī related it as a mursal report. And from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever recites Yā-Sīn by night or by day, no sin overtakes him that day.)) And from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Praise be to God, who has honoured me and honoured my community with Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and the Throne Verse, and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1).))

And Sahl [b.] ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī said: A man came to Ibrāhīm b. Adham and said: What do you say concerning Yā-Sīn? He said: Truly, in it there is a name — whoever knows it and calls upon God by it is answered, be he righteous or dissolute, when he calls upon it in the thing that is proper to it. He said: What do you say — may God set you aright — if I invoke with the whole sura? He said: No, not until you invoke with the very name itself, in the name that is proper to it. Do you not see that if you came to the shop of the apothecary while you had a disease, and you knew that your remedy was in the shop but did not know it specifically, and you took of everything that was in the shop and drank it for that [disease] — would it profit you, until you know that remedy itself and then use it as it ought to be used? And just as God created the disease and created for it the remedy and made it efficacious in it, so likewise to each name of the names of God there belongs something proper to it, with which one invokes in that matter, and he is answered on account of it.

The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((For everything there is a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is Yā-Sīn.)) And that suffices it for nobility, and [so too] the names that are in it…

…in greatness, since God, exalted is He, made it the heart of the Qurʾān. And the noblest of the members of the animal's body is the heart, and the power mingled with the heart is the noblest of powers. And it is, in the body of man, as the sun is to the world, by which life subsists; and that is because it gives life to the body, and is the wellspring of life and of breath and of heat ⟨and of breath and of the innate heat, and it is, of the body of man, as the sun⟩. And when its light is dispersed, the horizon grows dark, and everything of the animal grows still and sleeps. And these two powers are the two that resemble the two blasts which Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — blows into the Trumpet. And in the sun there is life for every plant in the earth and in the air, and the light of the moon and the splendour of the heaven. And no one has recited Sūrat Yā-Sīn and invoked with it while he was care-laden but that God relieved him of his care; nor any drowning man but that God, exalted is He, delivered him from drowning; nor any prisoner but that he was set free; nor any hungry man but that he was fed; nor any thirsty man but that his thirst was quenched; nor any fearful man but that he was made secure; nor any dead man but that God lightened the torment for him. And all this is from the nobility of the Name that is in it.

And it is related concerning Yā-Sīn that in it there is a name from among the names of God, glorified and exalted is He. /fol. 209v./ Whoever lights upon it by the secret of the letters, and writes it, and effaces it with pure water, facing the qibla, and drinks it for as many days as the number of the names — God causes him to speak with wisdom, and makes plain to him something of the secret of the worlds. And it is in the middle of the sura; and it is five words which sixteen letters make up, among them four dotted letters: two of them dotted from below and two from above. And that is by the secret of the natural, compositive, fourfold world. And likewise, if you multiply the four by itself, sixteen issues from it — and that is the sum of the names, I mean its letters. And by this secret the names appeared in it, in the heaven and the earth and the Footstool and Paradise; and by it the soul can be firmly established in the sensory world; and by it the secret ran through the world of the highest Dominion; and by it was ennobled the form of the heart that is in the secret. And that secret is not in Ṭā-Sīn; and that is because Ṭā-Sīn is joined in its meaning to the meaning of the sīn, whereas Yā-Sīn is not so, because the yāʾ falls in the inward. And this is what I have summarized from the gnostic.

For the repelling of the guile of enemies: His words, exalted is He, Truly We have set shackles upon their necks— down to His words, exalted is He — so they do not see (Q 36:8–9). These verses are for repelling the guile of enemies, and for turning back their harm and their destruction, and for turning away their faces, and for the blinding of their eyes, and for [the repelling of] their opposition. Whoever engraves them upon a shield, or engraves them upon a plate of copper or gold and nails it into the grip of the shield, and meets with it the enemies and those who oppose the religion — they are forsaken, and their guile is turned back upon them. And whoever recites them when he goes into his bed is safe that night from thieves and mischief-makers. And whoever recites them in a dispute between two men — the wrongdoer of the two is forsaken.

For security from fear: His words, exalted is He, "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). This is a verse of majestic worth, and in it is the Greatest Name of God. So if that is set down in a letter-square — and it is four by four — it is a security for every fearful person. And this is the form of its arrangement.

This noble verse — namely His words, exalted is He, "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord— this noble, majestic verse: in it is the Greatest Name of God, and it has, of number, 820. So if that is set down in a square, it is a security for every fearful person. And I have tried it many times, and I have not seen anything more successful than it in operation. And it is related also — he said: A man came to Ibrāhīm b. Adham and said: What do you say concerning Sūrat Yā-Sīn? He said: Truly, in it there are names — whoever knows them and calls upon God, exalted is He, by them does not ask God, exalted is He, for anything but that He gives it to him. /fol. 210r./
And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

And it is said that they are fourteen letters. Whoever draws them in a sixfold [figure] upon a signet of red gold, at the exaltation of the Sun and the Moon, increasing in light — its bearer sees of the traces of the subtlety of God, exalted is He, toward him what increases him in certainty, and he seeks no need but that he attains it. And if it is drawn with its eight appendages and carried, God, exalted is He, gives him kingship and leadership and high standing, and God, exalted is He, enriches him after destitution; and its benefits are many. And if one in pain, or one who has been stung, seals with it, he is healed forthwith, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And its benefits are for everything you seek: for the relieving of care, and the seeking of a livelihood, and acceptance, and high standing, and everything you desire — by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And one of the masters of free disposal (taṣarruf) said: no one writes this noble verse in a bowl of glass in the first [hour] of the day of Monday, at the beginning of the month, sixty times, and washes it off with rainwater and drinks it — for whatever matter he wishes to put out of mind — but that God uproots that matter from his heart, and makes him forget it, and turns it away from his thought, and expands his breast, and gives him his wish, and realizes his hope in what he purposed and hoped for.

And know that this lofty name and manifest secret has a square, mighty in station, dazzling in proof, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul), with Venus in her exaltation or in her house, in the first [hour] of the day of Friday, or the eighth. Its bearer sees of God's doing toward him, exalted is He, what descriptions are powerless to convey. So ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets.

And if you wish, you may write in the place of 136 His name, exalted is He, Muʾmin (the Granter of Security) — for it is among the most special of the attributes of the Prophet, our master Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace. And if you want, then write in the place of 135 His name, exalted is He, Musahhil (the Facilitator); and in the place of 129 His name, exalted is He, Laṭīf (the Subtle); and in the place of 130 His name, exalted is He, Munīl (the Bestower) — and it is among the most special of the attributes of Abraham, peace be upon him. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And know, O my brother — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that Sūrat Yā-Sīn is a magnificent sura, and that it has weighty occult properties that are not to be counted or numbered, because it is the heart of the Mighty Qurʾān, and the heart of this sura is "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). And we have already mentioned something of its occult properties; and I shall mention here something of its benefits and of what pertains to this noble sura. May God profit me and you by it. Amen.
So I say:
Faṣl: On the subjugation of hearts and on concord between those who hate one another

He writes them, as I shall explain to you, upon paper (kāghad), written with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water. Let the writing be in a felicitous hour; and let whoever wishes carry it, upon the name of whom he wishes and the name of his mother. And he recites the noble sura seven times and says: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura! — seven times; and you say: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, with the procuring and the attracting of the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] to the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Then let him carry the sheet with him, and he will see the wonder of wonders in the way of love and lasting affection between them, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among them also, for the deliverance of a prisoner: write the noble sura and what is with it of the names of God, exalted is He, upon a pure garment; and let the recitation be three times, and say in the course of the recitation: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, with the procuring of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right it has over you and by its being obeyed among you. Then spread dust upon something clean, such as a napkin or the like, and lay the dust out flat; and let the prisoner pray upon that dust two rakʿas, in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣfourteen times. And when he has given the salām you say: O God, I ask You, O God, O Sublime, O Lord of seven heavens. And he says: Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him who gives release to every prisoner! Glory be to Him who knows every hidden thing! Glory be to Him whose command is between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say "Be", and it is! So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned. Then let the dust be buried in a place that no foot treads upon; for the prisoner will be delivered speedily, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among the occult properties, for the repelling of diseases and ailments: write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water; and let it be dissolved with rainwater, and let the one who has the malady and the ailment drink it. And let him say when he drinks it: I have made the intention of healing by the mighty verses of God and His generous names. For God, exalted is He, heals him and gives him well-being from that malady and ailment, if God, glorified and exalted is He, wills. And it also benefits palpitation of the heart, and trembling from a sudden blow or from panic: he does that as we have mentioned at first.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties, for the prevention of sorcery and of harmful acts, and of what is feared and of what may befall him: if he wishes to prevent that, he writes the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass, with a pen of sweet basil (rayḥān); and the ink is what I shall mention — and it is a little rose-water, and water of sweet pomegranate, and myrtle-water, and jasmine-water, and water of vine-wood, and a little rainwater, and water of carrot leaves. A little of each thing is taken, and one writes with it; and it is dissolved with rainwater, and the bewitched man — or he who fears sorcery — bathes with it beside running water, or beside a channel that runs /fol. 211v./ toward the qibla. And he rubs the whole of his body except the front and the rear, for he must never touch them with his hand. And you recite, at his washing, His words, exalted is He: Moses said: What you have brought is sorcery; God will bring it to nothing. Truly God does not set right the work of those who work corruption (Q 10:81). O God, I ask You by the right of the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn that You repel from me the sorcery of the sorcerers and the guile of the guileful, by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". For God, exalted is He, takes away from him what he fears and what he guards against, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties, for the retention of the Qurʾān and of the rest of the sciences: you write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass, with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water; and it is set out beneath the sky, and drunk on an empty stomach. He does that seven consecutive days, and avoids during them the eating of what is sour and salty. And he says when he drinks it: O God, I ask You, O God, by the blessing of this noble sura and the blessed, eminent names, that You cause me to retain the Mighty Qurʾān and the noble knowledge; and all that You have taught to those whom You love — make me one of them; and what You have taught them, teach me, O God, O All-Knowing, O Wise. For God, exalted is He, teaches him the Qurʾān and whatever he wishes of the sciences, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties: whoever desires high standing with kings and viziers and rulers, let him write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass with oil of zanbaq (lily), and jasmine oil, and oil of nasrīn (eglantine), and balsam oil; and if the oil is not to be had, then with the waters of them, and a little Palestinian oil. And there is recited together with the sura And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31); and His words, exalted is He, and he was of high standing with God (Q 33:69); and the Throne Verse; and When the help of God comes, and the victory (Q 110:1); and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān), and the Fātiḥa. Then put what you have written into a phial. And when you want to go in upon a king or a ruler or a vizier to ask a need, anoint your face with a little of the oil that is in the phial, and recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn and what you have written. Then you go in upon whom you wish of the rulers; and you will attain with him rank, and favour, and great standing; and he will accomplish for you all your interests and whatever you seek, without weariness and without hardship, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Faṣl. And among the occult properties of this noble sura: it is recited for the increase of provisions and of good things. O You who give life to the dead and record what they have sent forward and their traces — and every thing We have enumerated in a clear register (Q 36:12)! And O You who give life to the earth after its death and bring forth from it grain, of which they eat! O You who placed in it gardens of date-palms and vines, and We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they might eat of its fruit — and their hands did not make it. Will they not then give thanks?(Q 36:34–35)! O You who are glorified with every tongue! And O Creator of all the pairs, of what the earth brings forth, and of themselves, and of what they do not know (Q 36:36)! O You who strip apart the night and the day, and behold, they are in darkness (Q 36:37)! O You who determined mansions for the sun — it runs to a resting-place appointed for it (Q 36:38) — O Mighty, O All-Knowing! O You who determined mansions for the moon, until it returns like an old palm-branch! It does not behove the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each swims in a sphere (Q 36:39–40)! O

You who carried us in the laden ship and created for us the like of it, in which they ride! And if You will, You drown them — and there is no crier for them, nor are they delivered, save by a mercy from Us and an enjoyment for a while (Q 36:43–44) — and there is no fleeing from Him. O Compassionate! O You who created for us cattle — and We have made them submissive to them, so that some of them are their mounts, and of some they eat (Q 36:72) — and appointed for us in them benefits and drinks! O You who created man from a drop — and behold, he is a manifest adversary (Q 36:77)! O You who give life to the bones when they are crumbled to dust! O You who brought them into being the first time, and who is All-Knowing of every creation (Q 36:79)! O You who made for us from the green tree fire, and behold, from it you kindle (Q 36:80)! O You who created the heavens and the earth! O Powerful, O Creator of all, O All-Knowing! O You who, when He wills a thing, [His command] is only that He say to it "Be", and it is (Q 36:82)! O All-Glorified, O All-Holy! O You in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to whom you shall be returned (Q 36:83)! /fol. 216r./

He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. His are the Most Beautiful Names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise (Q 59:23–24). So when you have resolved, then rely upon God; truly God loves those who rely [upon Him](Q 3:159). But if they turn away, then say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129).
And whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him. Truly God attains His purpose. God has appointed a measure for everything (Q 65:3).
O God, /fol. 216v./ incline toward me the hearts of Your servants, of the sons of Adam and the daughters of Eve, male and female, free and slave, great and small —

— with lasting love and affection and tenderness and mercy; and draw their hearts to me; and guard me from the evil of all that they conceal against me and desire for me; and ward off from me their guile and their harm and their evil, and the evil of what they conceal against me. I ask You, by the sanctity of what I have recited, that You show me Your sacred precinct through Your generosity, and that You bring me to the visitation of the grave of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, O God, O Lord of the worlds, I ask You: O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, O Peace, O Granter of Security, O Overseer, O Mighty, O Compeller, O Supremely Great, O Creator, O Maker, O Provider, O Opener, O All-Knowing, O Expander, O Sublime, O Giver of might, O Giver of abasement, O All-Hearing, All-Seeing, O Subtle, O Forbearing, O Magnificent, O Most Thankful, O Preserver, O Nourisher, O Bringer to Account, O Generous,

O Watcher, O Answerer, O All-Embracing, O Gatherer, O Self-Sufficient, O Enricher, O Abiding, O Light of everything and its guidance! You are He whose light cleaved the darknesses, the High, the Towering, above everything in exaltation. O God, I ask You, O God, that You make subject to me the servant-spirits (khuddām) of this noble sura, that they be a help to me in all that I seek and desire. Answer, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, and be a help to me in all that I seek and desire, by the right it has over you and its sanctity with you! Put your trust and rise up, by the right of the secrets that are within it! And whoever of you holds back is burnt with the Fire. Come now! Speed! Haste! This very hour! And whoever does not answer God's summoner cannot thwart [Him] on earth, and he has no protectors apart from Him (Q 46:32). Answer, and put your trust in what I have commanded you, by the right of this noble sura; and answer and obey — [by the right it has] over you and its sanctity with you. Haste! Speed! This very hour!
This noble invocation is now complete and finished. So know its worth, and what has reached you of it; and fear God, exalted is He; and know that God is with those who fear Him. So understand.

The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Yā-Sīn is for whatever it is recited for.)) And it is related from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn purely for the face of God, exalted is He, God forgives him what has gone before of his sin and what [is to come].)) And it is related from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((The secrets of God are in the Qurʾān; [and the secrets of] the Qurʾān are Sūrat Yā-Sīn; and the secrets of Sūrat Yā-Sīn are in four verses of it, among them His words, exalted is He, Truly the companions of the Garden this day are in an occupation, delighting (Q 36:55), down to His words, exalted is He, "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58).)) So ponder these secrets and consider them well; and God, exalted is He, is the Granter of success.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obeying Him and in understanding the secrets of His names — that I mention to you a second invocation for this noble sura, and its excellences, and its benefits, and its exalted secrets. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Yā-Sīn, Yā-Sīn, Yā-Sīn, Yā-Sīn, Yā-Sīn, Yā-Sīn. Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾān, truly you /fol. 217r./ are among the messengers, upon a straight path — a sending-down from the Mighty, the Compassionate — that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so that they are heedless. The word has already come true against most of them, so they do not believe. Truly We have set shackles upon their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so that their heads are forced back. And We have set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them over, so they do not see. It is all one to them whether you warn them or do not warn them: they will not believe. You warn only him who follows the Reminder and fears the All-Merciful in the unseen: so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward. Truly it is We who give life to the dead, and We write down what they have sent ahead and their traces; and everything We have reckoned up in a clear register (Q 36:1–12). Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him who gives release to every prisoner! Glory be to Him who makes it easy for every debtor! Glory be to Him who delivers every prisoner! Glory be to Him who knows every hidden thing! Glory be to Him who set the treasuries of His kingdom between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (Q 6:100). And peace be upon the messengers; and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:1–5).

And you say three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement, You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help — and he asks for his need. And you say seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). And you say: O God, make subject to me the kingdom and the dominion. There is no god but You, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By You I seek succour: O Succourer, succour me! — forty times; and it is answered for him on the spot. And you say thirty-seven times: O Answerer, answer my invocation and accomplish my need, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And you say: O God, make me of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those against whom there is wrath, and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names; O Lord, O All-Merciful, [make me] of those who fear their Lord in the unseen — so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward (Q 36:11). O God, give me good tidings, on the day of meeting You, of forgiveness from You and a generous reward. And he asks; it is answered on the spot. not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7) — Āmīn. And he says: Yā Mubīn (O Evident), Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn. And you say: I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your chosen Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — the generous, the honoured, that You deal with me as befits You, and that You do not deal with me as I deserve; truly You are worthy to be feared and worthy to forgive. And he asks for his need; it is answered on the spot. And you say: And strike for them a similitude: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it; when We sent to them two, and they gave the lie to them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: Truly we are messengers to you. They said: You are only mortals like ourselves, and the All-Merciful /fol. 217v./ has sent down nothing; you are only lying. They said: Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you; and upon us is only the clear delivering of the message (Q 36:13–17). Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him who gives release to every prisoner! Glory be to Him who makes it easy for every debtor! Glory be to Him who delivers every prisoner! Glory be to Him who knows every hidden thing! Glory be to Him the treasuries of whose kingdom are between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (Q 6:100). And peace be upon the messengers; and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:1–5).

And you say three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement, You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help — and he asks for his need; it is answered for him on the spot. And you say seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). O God, make me of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names; and make me, O Lord, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, of those who fear their Lord in the unseen — so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward (Q 36:11). O God, give me good tidings, on the day of meeting You, of forgiveness from You and a generous reward. And he asks for his need; it is answered on the spot. not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7) — Āmīn. Yā Mubīn (O Evident), Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn. And he says four times: I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your chosen Prophet Muḥammad the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — the generous, the most generous, that You deal with me as befits You, and that You do not deal with me as I deserve. Truly You are worthy, and worthy to forgive. And he asks for his need; it is answered for him on the spot. O God, make subject to me the kingdom and the dominion. O [You beside whom] there is no god but You, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By You I seek succour: O Succourer, succour me! — forty times. Then he asks for his need; it is answered for him on the spot. They said: We augur ill of you; if you do not desist we shall surely stone you, and a painful torment shall touch you from us (Q 36:18). In this place there is a mighty secret against an enemy: you draw a figure upon the ground, and in your hand is a knife of steel without blades (bilā nuṣūl); and you say seventeen times, and you strike upon the said figure — you will see a wonder, and God knows best — from every side: They said: Your ill augury is with you. Is it because you were reminded? Nay, you are a people gone to excess. And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running /fol. 218r./ who said: O my people, follow the messengers! Follow those who ask of you no wage, and who are rightly guided. And why should I not worship Him who originated me, and to whom you shall be returned? Shall I take, apart from Him, gods whose intercession, if the All-Merciful should intend me some harm, would avail me nothing, and who could not deliver me?(Q 36:19–23). O God, preserve me from every affliction in this world and from torment in the hereafter. O God, do not change my name, and do not alter my body, and do not part me from Your Prophet and Your beloved Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. And God created every crawling creature from water: of them there are those that go upon their belly, and of them there are those that go upon two legs, and of them there are those that go upon four. God creates what He wills; truly God is powerful over everything (Q 24:45). Then he prostrates; then he asks and seeks his need and names it. And this is for the repelling of pains and sicknesses and for the healing of the sick: Truly then I should be in manifest error (Q 36:24). Yā Mubīn (O Evident), Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn, Yā Mubīn. Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him who gives release to every prisoner! Glory be to Him who makes it easy for every debtor! Glory be to Him who delivers every prisoner! Glory be to Him who knows every hidden thing! Glory be to Him the treasuries of whose kingdom are between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (Q 6:100). And peace be upon the messengers; and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:1–5).

And he says three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement, You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help — and he asks. And you say seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). O God, make me of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names, all of them; and make me, O Lord, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, of those who fear their Lord in the unseen — so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward (Q

36:11). O God, give me good tidings, on the day of meeting You, of forgiveness from You and a generous reward. Then he seeks and asks for his need; and it is answered on the spot. Truly I have believed in your Lord, so hear me. It was said: Enter the Garden. He said: Would that my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and set me among the honoured (Q 36:25–27). And he says eleven times: O You who honoured Your believing servants, honour me with the honour of Your near-brought friends and Your righteous servants, those upon whom there is no fear, nor shall they grieve (Q 10:62). O God, honour me with the accomplishing of [my] needs, out of the overflow of Your bounty, O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, by the right of this noble sura! /fol. 218v./ O Possessor of Majesty and Honour (37 times). O our God and God of everything, one God — there is no god but You. O Living, O Self-Subsisting (41 times). O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour! O God, honour me out of the overflow of Your bounty and Your generosity with what befits You in the two abodes; truly You are powerful over everything. Then he asks for his need and names it: O Living, O Self-Subsisting, by You I seek succour; O Succourer, succour me, and set right for me my whole affair, and do not entrust me to myself, nor to anyone other than You, for the blink of an eye, nor for less than that nor for more. And guide me to the straight path, the path of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Surely to God all affairs come home (Q 42:53) — eleven times. Accomplish my need, O Fulfiller of needs — three times. O Answerer, O Answerer, O Answerer, answer my invocation, O Answerer of invocations, O Most Merciful of the merciful — thirty-seven times. O God, bless our master Muḥammad, and the family of our master Muḥammad, and his companions and his kin, all of them, by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Magnificent". O Fulfiller of needs, accomplish my need — seventeen times. Then he asks for his need; it is answered on the spot. And We did not send down upon his people, after him, any host from heaven, nor were We sending down. It was but a single cry, and behold, they were extinguished (Q 36:28–29) — here he mentions his enemy. Whenever they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it; and they hasten about the earth in corruption, and God does not love the workers of corruption (Q 5:64). O God, quench his evil away from me, and extinguish his guile, and untie his knots, and annul his affair, and cut short his life. If We will, We shall send down upon them a sign from heaven, and their necks will stay bowed low before it (Q 26:4) — three times; and he strikes the ground with his hand three times. Afterwards he draws his image upon the ground at his right and strikes it with his right hand, saying: khādimūn, khādimūn, khādimūn ("servants"). Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but that they mock him (Q 36:30). God mocks them, and gives them rein to wander blindly in their insolence (Q 2:15). Truly We have sufficed you against the mockers (Q 15:95) —

I am sufficed against the evil of So-and-so — you say it three times. Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, and that they do not return to them?(Q 36:31). O Destroyer of the generations that are past among the nations gone by, So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] cannot thwart You! O Destroyer of the wrongdoers, O Extirpator of the transgressors, destroy my enemies with the destruction of him whom You destroyed for his wrongdoing! O Destroyer of the tyrants of old in the generations that have vanished, destroy my enemy So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] with that wherewith You destroy the wrongdoing folk! And truly We are able to show you what We promise them (Q 43:42) (3 times). Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, and that they do not return to them?(Q 36:31) (3 times). And each and every one of them shall surely be brought before Us (Q 36:32). O God, bring present to me the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and his hearing and his sight and his inmost heart, upon love of me, so that he neither sees nor hears nor speaks save with love of me. O Gatherer of mankind for a day about which there is no doubt /fol. 219r./ — truly God does not fail the appointed promise (Q 3:9), gather between me and the senses of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] upon love of me, and join between me and him as You joined between snow and fire! O God, set me in [high] standing with him, by the making known of the bonds of affinity (al-ulfāt) gathered before the parting: 46468642 — he says it 20 times.

And each and every one of them shall surely be brought before Us (Q 36:32). And I cast upon you love from Me, that you might be fashioned under My eye (Q 20:39). They love them as they should love God; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined between their hearts; but God joined between them. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). O You who joined between snow and fire, join between the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]! O Mighty, O Compeller! And a sign for them is the dead earth: We gave it life and brought forth from it grain, so that they eat of it. And We placed in it gardens of date-palms and vines, and We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they may eat of its fruit — and it was not their hands that made it. Will they not then give thanks? Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth brings forth, and of themselves, and of what they do not know. And a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it, and behold, they are in darkness (Q 36:33–37). And he says: I have struck the neck of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — God is greatest! I have cut off the head of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] with the sword of God the All-Subduing. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off; and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 6:45).

And he recites this supplication of cutting off (duʿāʾ al-qaṭʿ). He says: O God, You are the One who encompasses the unseen of every witnessed thing, the One who has mastery over everything inward and outward. I ask You, O God, O God, O God, O Most Merciful of the merciful, O God, O Most Merciful toward tears, O Remover of distresses! You are God who dispels the cloud of trials when it has grown heavy; who clears away the mist of rancours when it has trailed its skirts; who makes their sown crop like chaff and their bones like decayed remains; who turns the vanquished into the victor and the sought after into the seeker. My God, how many a servant has called upon You: Truly I am vanquished, so give victory!(Q 54:10) — and We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down, and made the earth gush forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed; and We bore him upon a thing of planks and nails (Q 54:11–13). O Lord, O Lord, I am vanquished, so give victory! God is greatest! — and he strikes the ground with his hand three times together with "God is greatest, God is greatest, God is greatest". I ask You, O You whose power is subduing, and whose signs are dazzling, and whose retributions are severing, and for every tyrant a crushing [blow] — I ask You by the power whereby You are the owner of their souls, so that were You to seize them they would be snuffed out; and in Your grasp are the stuffs of their breaths, so that were You to sever them they would be frozen where they are. What, then, prevents You, O Lord, from restraining their might, and stilling their breaths, and stripping from them the garment of Your protection, leaving them bare of their safety from You? From You is Your severe seizing-grip! Upon the earth they rejoice, and in the arena of transgression against Your servants they frolic. O God, bless

Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and grant benediction and peace. O God, where is Your sufficing against him who has wronged me, O Crusher of the tyrants and of the arrogant, O Cutter-off of the last remnant of the mocking tyrants (al-farāʿina)? How swift is the descent, and how swift the alighting of Your glorious subduing upon every obstinate tyrant and rebellious devil who has transgressed against the servants, and behaved insolently /fol. 219v./ in the lands, and hastened about with corruption! Truly You are God: by You I seek succour, my God, against him who has wronged me. And he says: My Master, [I ask You] that You help me against him who has made war on me; and that You rout for me him who has come out against me; and that You subdue him who has fought me; and that You forsake my enemies and rout them; and give them turbid water to drink, and make them fuel for Gehenna; and send upon their gardens a reckoning from heaven, so that it becomes a slippery bare slope, or its water sinks into the ground so that you can never seek it out (Q 18:40–41). You are the Compeller, the Supremely Great, the Constrictor, the Helper, the Strong, the Prevailer, the All-Subduing, the Giver of abasement, the Avenger, the Destroyer, the Severe, the Forsaker, the Deferrer, the Withholder, the Constrictor, the Expander, the Preserver, the Bringer of Harm, the Crusher, and the Possessor of Strength, the Firm. Then you strike the ground with your hand and you say "God is greatest" three times: So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off; and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 6:45). Help me against him who has wronged me! So God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God (Q 40:21). So they lay prostrate in their dwellings (Q 7:78). O God, seize him, and forsake him, and destroy him! God is greatest! The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it (Q 16:1). And the sun runs to a resting-place appointed for it: that is the determining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. And the moon — We have determined mansions for it, until it returns like an old withered palm-stalk. It does not befit the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each in an orbit is swimming. And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship. And We created for them the like of it, in which they ride (Q 36:38–42).
And there is written, for the drowning [of a ship], upon one of the planks of the vessel you wish to sink — as you see — nine ṭāʾs; and say: O letter ṭāʾ, blot out! — nine times.

And if We will, We drown them, and there is no cry for help for them, nor are they delivered — save by a mercy from Us, and as an enjoyment for a while (Q 36:43–44). You write it upon a piece of pitch, and it is stuck fast in the ship, at its bottom; then, if it sails on that day, it either sinks or splits open. And it is written upon a new red potsherd and cast into the ship; then nothing of the calamities will ever befall that ship.
And when it is said to them: Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that you may obtain mercy — and no sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it…

…averse to it; and when it is said to them, "Spend of that which God has provided you", those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom, if God willed, He would feed? You are in nothing but manifest error"(Q 36:45–47). These verses are for the easing of provision. They are recited thirty-seven times; it is answered on the spot. And he says: Glory to Him who gives relief to every one who grieves; glory to Him who gives respite to every prisoner; glory to Him who makes things easy for every debtor; glory to Him who delivers every prisoner; glory to Him who knows every hidden thing; glory to Him who has set the treasuries of His dominion between the kāf and the nūn; so glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:83). Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (cf. Q 37:180); and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:1–5). Then he asks; it is answered on the spot. And he says seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path /fol. 220r./, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). O God, make me one of those upon whom You have bestowed favour and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names, O Lord of the worlds, O All-Merciful! Not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray. Amen (Q 1:7). O Mubīn (the Evident), O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn — seven times. O God, subject to me the kingdom and the dominion! O You beside whom there is no god, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By You I seek succour: O Succourer, succour me! — four times. And he asks his need; it is answered him on the spot. I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your honoured Prophet, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — that You deal with me as befits You, and not deal with me as befits me; truly You are the One worthy to be held in awe and worthy to forgive. And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?" They await only a single cry that will seize them while they are yet disputing; then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families (Q 36:48–50). This verse is for driving an enemy out of a town: when it is recited over his name and his mother's name, he departs to a town other than it.

And the trumpet is blown, and at once they are hastening forth from the graves to their Lord. They say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping-place? This is what the All-Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth." It was but a single cry, and behold, they were all arraigned before Us (Q 36:51–53). This verse is for the summoning of the kings of the jinn: when you recite it, it is for them a mighty compelling formula (zajr). And you say with it: And the jinn know well that they shall be arraigned (Q 37:158).

This is Hell, which you were promised. Roast in it this day, for that you disbelieved (Q 36:63–64). This verse is written upon the forehead of the afflicted, and he rises up; and upon the epileptic (maṣrūʿ), and he speaks, and the companion-spirit (qarīn) talks upon his tongue.

This day We seal their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they used to earn. And if We willed, We would obliterate their eyes, and they would race to the path — but how would they see? And if We willed, We would transform them in their places, so that they could not go forward, nor return (Q 36:65–67). Or like the darknesses in a deep sea covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud — darknesses one above another; when he puts out his hand, he can scarcely see it. And he for whom God has appointed no light — for him there is no light (Q 24:40). These verses are for the return of a runaway slave. Sūrat Yā-Sīn is recited up to His words, exalted is He, so that they could not go forward (Q 36:67); and you recite Or like the darknesses in a deep sea (Q 24:40) — the verse. And you say: Truly He is able to bring him back, on the day when the secrets are tried; then he shall have no strength and no helper (Q 86:8–10), three times. His bewilderment is the bewilderment of the sparrow in the cage, hemmed in, overpowered.

And whomever We give long life, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?(Q 36:68). And he says: O God, I ask You, O God, by the rank of /fol. 220v./ Your Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — that You accomplish my need and bestow upon me my request and my desire. It is answered you on the spot. And We did not teach him poetry, nor would it befit him. It is only a remembrance and a clear Qurʾān (Q 36:69). Glory to Him who gives relief to every one who grieves; glory to Him who gives respite to every prisoner; glory to Him who makes things easy for every debtor; glory to Him who delivers every prisoner; glory to Him who knows every hidden thing; glory to Him who has set the treasuries of His dominion between the kāf and the nūn; glory to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command] is only that He say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (cf. Q 37:180); and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:1–7). And he says three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement! You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. And he says seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). O God, make me one of those upon whom You have bestowed favour and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names, O Lord of the worlds, O All-Merciful — three times. And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. Not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray. Amen (Q 1:7). [O Mubīn] — seven times. And you say: O God, subject to me the kingdom and the dominion! O You beside whom there is no god, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By You I seek succour: O Succourer, succour me! — he says it forty times, and he asks his need; it is answered him on the spot. He says thirty-seven times: O Answerer, O Answerer, O Answerer, answer my invocation and accomplish my need, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful! I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your venerated, honoured Prophet, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — that You deal with me as befits You, and not deal with me as befits me; truly You are the One worthy to be held in awe and worthy to forgive. And he says: that he may warn whoever is alive, and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers. Have they not seen that We created for them, of what

Our hands have made, cattle, of which they are the owners? And We have made them submissive to them, so that some of them are their mounts, and of some they eat. And in them they have benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?(Q 36:70–73). This verse is for the riding-beast: when — and if — it, or any of the beasts, proves refractory to you, you say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not equal to it; and truly to our Lord we are returning (Q 43:13–14). And if We will, We shall send down upon them a sign from heaven, so that their necks remain humbled before it — so that their necks remain humbled before it (Q 26:4). And in the cattle there is surely a lesson for you: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, from between dung and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers (Q 16:66); and a tree issuing from Mount Sinai, which bears oil /fol. 221r./ and a relish for those who eat (Q 23:20); so God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137).

And you say: And they have taken gods besides God, that perhaps they might be helped. They are not able to help them, though they are for them an army brought forward. So let not their speech grieve you; truly We know what they conceal and what they proclaim (Q 36:74–76). O Lord, I ask You by Your name with which You opened the world of creation and of command, by the self-disclosure to the Real that makes manifest relations, and the Transcendent in command, in existence, and in hiddenness, intelligible [and] sensible — that being known to him to whom You have made it appear, unknown to him whom You have made to witness it, [and] to whomever You will, by what in it is ambiguous: a multiplicity that does not impugn the unity of what You have made firm of the firmly established. O All-Knowing, O Wise, O Opener, O God, O Lord! And I ask You by Your name, O God, by the secret of the sending-down: the relational bond linking the Presence of Necessity and that of Possibility, which requires the manifestation of the greatest attribute by the ambiguous Name, for the establishment of the two modes of divinity, in general and in particular, at the outset and at the return; from the amplitude of the all-embracing all-mercifulness (raḥmāniyya), which has no end in settledness and in fixity; from the effusion proper to the compassionateness (raḥīmiyya) that raises up for the witnessing of the affirmation of drawing near, by a nearness whose quiddity is unknown, from You. O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, O Opener, O All-Knowing! I ask You for illumination, for facilitation, for aid, for discernment, for completion, for the drawing of provision and of blessing therein, for hope and good opinion of You, and for despair of all besides You. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate — [as] a bringing-into-being of Your command, a completing of Your munificence, and a blessing from You. Blessed is Your name, and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You. In You we have believed, to You we have surrendered, and upon You we have relied. Realize us, O God, by Your light and by the light of Your command; and make us absent from all besides You, in oblivion in You, O God, in witnessing of You, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate! "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). Whoever has a need, let him persevere in the recitation of this blessed supplication, for it will accomplish his need by the leave of God, exalted is He. Whoever wants that, let him pray two rakʿas: he recites in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa and When the help of God comes, and the victory (Q 110:1); and after it he recites the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and seals with this blessed supplication and asks. It is answered him on the spot, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And he says: Has man not seen that We created him from a drop? Then, behold, he is a manifest adversary!(Q 36:77). Glory to Him who gives relief to every one distressed; glory to Him who gives respite to every prisoner; glory to Him who makes things easy for every debtor; glory to Him who knows every hidden thing; glory to Him the treasuries of whose dominion are between the kāf and the nūn; glory to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command] is only that He say "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (cf. Q 37:180); and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us…

…the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:6–7). [And he says three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement! You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. And he says seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7).] O God, make me one of those upon whom You have bestowed favour and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names, O Lord, O All-Merciful — three times. And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. Not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray. Amen (Q 1:7). O Mubīn (the Evident), O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn. And you say: O God, subject to me the kingdom and the dominion! O You beside whom there is no god, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By You I seek succour: O Succour of those who seek succour, O Succourer, succour me! — forty times; and he asks his need; it is answered him on the spot. And thirty-seven times: O Answerer, answer my invocation and accomplish my need, O Most Merciful of the merciful (4 times). He says: I ask You by

Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your venerated, honoured Prophet, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — that You deal with me as befits You, and not deal with me as befits me; truly You are the One worthy to be held in awe and worthy to forgive. And he seeks his need; it is answered on the spot. And he says: And he has struck for Us a likeness, and forgotten his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to the bones when they are decayed?" Say: "He will give them life who brought them forth the first time, and He is Knower of every creation — He who has made for you fire out of the green tree, and behold, from it you kindle." Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes indeed — and He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing (Q 36:78–81). O God, lighten from us the weight of the burdens [of sin], and provide us with the livelihood of the righteous; and suffice us, and turn away from us the evil of the whisperings of the night and the day; and set free our necks, and the necks of our fathers and our mothers, from the Fire, by Your mercy, O Mighty, O Ever-Forgiving, O Generous, O Veiler! And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. He says: His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Glory be to Him, glory be to Him, glory be to Him! Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe (cf. Q 37:180); and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 37:181–182).

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:1–7). [And he says three times: O Master of the Day of Judgement! You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.] And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. And he says seven times: O Guide of those who go astray, there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7). O God, make me one of those upon whom You have bestowed favour and whom You have made to possess the secrets of Your names, O Lord, O All-Merciful; and make me one of those who fear their Lord in the unseen — so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward (Q 36:11). /fol. 222r./ Then he asks; it is answered on the spot. And he says: Not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7). O Mubīn (the Evident), O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn, O Mubīn. And he says: O God, subject to me the kingdom and the dominion! O You beside whom there is no god, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Living, O Self-Subsisting — three times. By You I seek succour, O God! O Succourer, succour me! — forty times; and he asks his need; it is answered him on the spot. And thirty-seven times: O Answerer, answer my invocation and accomplish my need and bring me to my request, O Most Merciful of the merciful — four times. I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by Your venerated, honoured, most honoured Prophet, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — that You deal with me as befits You, and not deal with me as befits me; truly You are the One worthy to be held in awe and worthy to forgive. And he asks his need; it is answered on the spot. And he says: O God, provide us with the good of this world and the bliss of the hereafter; and turn away from us the evil of this world and the terrors of the hereafter; and relent toward us before death; and do not torment us after death; and make light for us the throes of death, O Hearer of every voice! O God, preserve us from illness in a strange land, and from want in the time of hardship, and from wretchedness at the final end. O God, keep us safe and keep our religion safe; and do not strip our faith from us at the moment of the death-agony; and do not put us to trial at our dying. O God, make me abundant in Your remembrance, discharging what is due to You, hoping for Your promise, fearing Your threat, content with You in every state; and relieve my anxiety, and turn away my grief; and accomplish my need, O Fulfiller of needs; and answer my invocation, O Answerer of invocations, by the truth of this noble sura and this noble adjuration; and that You forgive me, and all Muslim men and Muslim women and believing men and believing women, the living among them and the dead. Truly You are Hearing, Near, the Answerer of invocations — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

And let him be certain of the swiftness of the answer from God, exalted is He, before he rises from the place in which he recites. And by God, a great many people, beyond counting, have tried it. They all said: We invoked with the noble sura and the noble name — which is "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58) — together with the recitation of the noble name according to its complete number, 818; and they did not rise from their place until their needs were accomplished. So I swear by God — and by God, it has been tried in many places, not restricted [to one], but rather whenever he wishes. And try it, so that you may have the knowledge of certainty [and] the eye of certainty. And all this is together with truthfulness of intention and pure devotion toward God, mighty and majestic, at the time of the supplication.

And in the noble hadith, from God, mighty and majestic: ((I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he will.)) So when he has recited and God, exalted is He, has accomplished his need, let him recite all the formulae of praise (taḥmīdāt) that are in the Mighty Qurʾān, and give thanks to God, glorified and exalted. /fol. 222v/ And whoever wants ampleness of provision, let him recite it seven times every day and persevere in that: God will open for him seventy doors of provision. And he recites with it Sūrat al-Fatḥseven times, and al-Wāqiʿa seven times, and Have We not expanded (Q 94:1) seven times, and When the help of God comes, and the victory (Q 110:1) seven times. That will come to pass; and God, exalted is He, is the Guide to what is right.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — that I here mention the spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) of "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). It is that you begin, with the help of God, glorified and exalted, with a fast of forty days, beginning on the day of Sunday > and you recite His name, glorified and exalted; and so, a fast of forty days, beginning on the day of Sunday < when the first of the month falls on a Sunday. You recite the name after every prayer four hundred and thirty-two times. You shall not sleep of the night save a little, and you shall be in a fitting retreat (khalwa) in which you hear neither the barking of a dog nor the braying of an ass; and your food and drink shall be qulūbāt [a foodstuff], sugar, and oil. And guard yourself against everything possessed of a soul, and against whatever comes forth from a soul. And evening and morning, the suffumigation is such as aloeswood, nadd, ghāliya, and grains of Javanese benzoin (ḥaṣā lubān jāwī). And your garments and your body shall be pure; and every three days you bathe and perfume your garments with musk-scented perfume. And you recite the adjuration whose mention comes hereafter once after the dawn prayer, once after the forenoon prayer, and once before the setting of the sun. And when twenty days of the term have passed over you, there comes upon you one of the servant-spirits (khuddām), who says to you: O son of Adam, turn back from this name, and take for yourself of wealth what suffices you and brings you through — and he goes to great lengths with you in speech. But do not accept from him; and persevere in the litany of remembrance until the forty are complete. And every day he sees righteous dreams. Then, after the completion of the forty days, the house fills with light, and you look at the walls and at the place; and the walls of the house you are in are inscribed with "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). And the king enters, riding, with servant-spirits about him past all bearing. He says: Peace be upon you. So rise to your feet, and return the greeting to him, and say: May God ennoble you and make you mighty, O king, as you have ennobled me; and may God make you mighty as you have made me mighty. Now, O king, I want from you a sign, a means whereby I may attain to your presence. And he takes the further covenant from you, and stipulates conditions upon you: that you shall not lie, and shall not fall into disobedience. Then, if you have a need, he accomplishes it — even were it in the farthest part of the Yemen, or in the farthest part of Iraq, or in India; or something of wealth, and the conveyance [of it] from one place to a distant place; or whatever you want of pressing needs — it is accomplished by the leave of God, exalted is He.

This is the mighty adjuration, which you recite three times every day. You say: There are not in heaven revolutions, nor in the earth floods, nor in the mountains clods, nor in the seas drops, nor in the clouds motions, nor in the eyes glances, nor in souls stirrings of thought, but that they are abased before You, and witnesses for You, and pointing to You, and in /fol. 223r./ Your kingdom made subject by Your subjection of everything. Subject to me Your servants and Your angels, that I may seek help through them in what pleases You; and You are the One whose help is sought. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the
High, the Mighty. And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant peace.

And among the occult properties of the supplication of the noble Yā-Sīn: in it is the Greatest Name of God. It is that with which Jesus — peace be upon him — invoked, by which he used to bring the dead to life by the leave of God, exalted is He; and it is written in the heart of the Sun. No one has recited the noble sura but that God, exalted is He, raised him beyond what he seeks; and were he to adjure a dead man [by it], he would rise up alive by the leave of God, exalted is He. And it is this supplication:
O God, I ask You, O God, by the truth of the sura Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾān (Q 36:1–2), O Sender of the messengers, and Guide of whom He wills to a straight path…

1. To break a spell (siḥr): tie two hundred and two easily-untied knots along a cord about a meter and a half long. Set a glass full of water before the bewitched person. Let the bewitched person take the knotted cord in hand, recite the Basmala together with Surat al-Falaq, blow on the first knot, and untie it at once. While untying the knot he says: "I have undone the sorcery worked upon me." Next he recites the Basmala together with Surat al-Nās, blows on the second knot, and unties it at once. While untying it he says: "I have undone the sorcery worked against me." In this way, reciting the Basmala together with Surat al-Falaq and Surat al-Nās and untying every knot, he then drops the cord into the water in the glass. After the bewitched person has drunk this water, burn the cord in a fire. Once he has drunk the water, the bewitched person feels a great lightness and joy come over him. As time passes he will observe, by the leave of Allah, that he has been restored to his former health. This practice has been tried many times over and is sound; many people have been delivered from the effect of sorcery through it. Its worth should be recognized, and it should not be withheld from those who are bewitched. Reciting the noble Basmala at the start is sufficient — it need not be repeated afterward.
But while the recitation is taking place, someone else should, at intervals, burn uzerlik (wild rue) incense.

If someone who struggles with worship continues to recite this sūra, their laziness in worship will pass and their life will begin to improve.
